Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National “We shouldn’t only open pure water factories, we need factories to process raw materials” – President Mahama Source : Albert Kuzor 16 November 2026 6:00pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
President John Dramani Mahama has urged Ghanaian entrepreneurs to move beyond investing in sachet water production and establish factories that process the country's raw agricultural materials into finished products for local consumption and export.
He said Ghana had established enough pure water factories and must now prioritise industries that could transform its agricultural resources into products with higher economic value.
President Mahama said the country needed to change its approach to investment and industrial development.
“We shouldn't only open pure water factories. We have enough pure water factories. We need factories that will process our raw materials for export. We need factories that will create jobs for our people,” he said at the commissioning of EXIM Bank-funded NADKANSCO Cashew Processing Limited in Techiman on Monday, November 16, 2026.
The President argued that Ghana could generate more employment and wealth by processing its agricultural produce locally instead of exporting raw commodities and importing finished products.
He urged Ghanaian investors to take advantage of opportunities in agro-processing and manufacturing, insisting that the responsibility for industrialisation should not be left to foreign investors.
“We must change that mindset. We are not a country of traders. We are a country of manufacturers,” he said.
President Mahama maintained that local entrepreneurs had the financial capacity to establish factories and contribute to the country's industrial transformation.
“All these factories that are being built, Ghanaians can build them. They are Ghanaians who have the resources to be able to build them,” he added.
He cited maize, rice and mangoes as some of the agricultural commodities with significant potential for processing, urging investors to establish factories to produce maize flour, process rice for local consumption and export, and manufacture mango juice.
“I want to see more NADKANSCOs, not only processing cashew, but processing many other things. Processing maize flour, processing rice for local consumption and export, processing mangoes for juice for local consumption and export. There's so much that we can do,” he said.
The President said the government's new economy agenda was designed to channel investments into productive sectors capable of creating employment and expanding the country's industrial base.
He disclosed that government would invest $10 billion of its own resources in eight strategic sectors, including agriculture and agribusiness, to stimulate production and create jobs.
The commissioning of the NADKANSCO cashew processing factory, he said, demonstrated the government's commitment to adding value to locally produced commodities and expanding Ghana's manufacturing capacity.
